# fastf 3.5.0 — the app answers the keys you try

The terminal app had grown a key for everything and a grammar for nothing. Some
lists paged and some did not. `g` was "first row" on one screen and "make a
template from a folder" on the next. `←` and `→` did nothing at all, anywhere.
And the app never moved: a batch tagged ten projects and the frame afterwards
was the frame before, except for ten cells nobody was watching.

This release is about the two things you do most and notice least — moving
around, and seeing what changed.

## Every list moves the same way

The project table, the detail pane, the templates tab, the action menu, the
template builder, the settings, and any dialog with more in it than fits:

| | |
|---|---|
| `↑` `↓` or `k` `j` | a row, wrapping at the ends |
| PgUp / PgDn | a screenful, stopping at the ends |
| **Ctrl-U / Ctrl-D** | half a screenful |
| Home / End or `g` `G` | the first row, the last row |

Before this, the page keys stopped short of the action menu and the builder,
and the jumps stopped short of the templates tab as well — so the two lists you
cannot search were the two you could only walk one row at a time.

## `→` goes in, `←` comes back

One rule, everywhere: **`→` (or `l`) opens whatever is under the cursor** — the
same thing Enter does where you are — and **`←` (or `h`) leaves one level**.
On a project it opens the action menu; on the templates tab it opens the
builder; in the builder it opens a section; in the settings it edits the row.
Coming back out works the same way from all of them, and from the detail pane
and the templates tab it goes back to where you came from.

`←` never quits. On the project list there is nothing above it, so it does
nothing at all — leaving is Esc's job, and Esc's alone.

The whole app can now be driven with the four arrow keys.

## Keys that meant two things

Since there is no installed base to break, the collisions are simply gone:

- `g` and `G` are the first and last row **everywhere**. The templates tab's two
  verbs moved: `I` makes a template from a folder, `H` opens the guide.
- `Ctrl-U` is half a page up. "Clear the search" gave up that key — Esc's first
  step already clears the query, and inside the search bar `Ctrl-U` has always
  meant "delete to the start of the line", one keystroke away from meaning
  something else.
- **Ctrl-C is in the help now.** The key that cancels a running job appeared in
  no help, no hint bar and no command palette.
- Pressing `?` in the search bar types a question mark, and the hint bar there
  no longer claims otherwise. In any text field the app now advertises only the
  keys that actually fire — `F1` for help, `Ctrl-P` for the palette.

## Four things it could not do

- **Mark a run of rows.** Space marks a row and steps on; **`v`** marks
  everything between the last row you marked and the cursor. Twenty rows are
  three keystrokes instead of twenty.
- **Sort both ways.** `size reversed` is the smallest first, `id reversed` is
  the highest ID first, and name, template and base all run backwards too. `S`
  lists both directions of each.
- **Filter by tag** from the command palette: it writes `tag:whatever` into the
  search bar, which is what a tag filter is — so clearing it is the same
  keystroke as clearing any other search.
- **`/` narrows the settings screen** to the setting you are looking for, by its
  name, its value or the `config set` key. The title says what it is narrowed
  to; Esc gives the whole screen back.

## The app moves now, where movement means something

Four things, and nothing else:

- **A row a verb just changed lights up** for about half a second. A batch tags
  ten projects while your cursor is on one of them — this is how you see which
  ten.
- **A size cell lights up as its number lands**, so a table filling in reads as
  news rather than as a reflow.
- **One spinner**, the same everywhere something is pending.
- **A message dims for its last half second**, so it reads as going rather than
  as a line that vanished.

No sliding dialogs, no eased scrolling, no cursor trails: they answer no
question, and this app's rule for motion is the rule it already had for colour
— it appears where it *means* something.

`fastf config set motion off` turns all of it off; `FASTF_MOTION=0` does the
same for one run; a palette with no colour is always off. The app still costs
nothing while idle — the faster wake lasts exactly as long as something is
actually moving.

One thing this fixed along the way: the spinner used to **stop turning while the
app was busiest**. A tick was a quiet interval rather than a deadline, so a
stream of work restarted it and the one indicator that says "still going" went
still.

## Nothing else changed

No flag, no config file format, no template format. `state.toml` records the
sort direction as well as the order, and every file written before this still
parses. One new setting, `motion`.

Full key list: [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/cli.md#keys)
